questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: Position yourself so other drivers can see you as early as possible.
Always stay in the left lane to avoid oncoming traffic.
Slowly creep up to the intersection.
Weave slightly so your headlight is more visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position yourself so other drivers can see you as early as possible.
questions.explanation: Move to the part of your lane where oncoming drivers will see you first. For example, if a corner is to your right, stay on the left side of your lane so drivers can spot you sooner.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you avoid other drivers' blind spots.
Help you stay hidden from other drivers.
Make it easier for others to see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you stay hidden from other drivers.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen. It keeps you out of other drivers' blind spots, avoids road hazards, shows your intentions, protects you from wind blasts, and gives you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid riding over an obstacle, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down as much as possible.
Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Stay on your seat and lift your feet off the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as much as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down and hit the obstacle at a 90-degree angle if possible. Keep your motorcycle upright. Just before hitting the obstacle, ease off the throttle to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
It does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects your entire face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face during a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes, not your face. A windshield cannot replace a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: How should you make a quick stop on wet pavement?
questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes during a quick stop on slippery pavement. The front brake is safe to use on slippery surfaces if you apply it gradually to prevent locking.

questions.question: Which of the following is typically a rectangular sign?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering or symbols. Riders must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.correctAnswerText: All day and night.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during daylight. Wearing bright colors and reflective materials at all times makes you more visible and safer.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
It does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects your entire face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face during a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes, not your face. A windshield is not a good substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: How much following distance should you normally keep from the vehicle ahead?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if road or weather conditions are poor.

questions.question: A proper lane position can help you do all of the following, except:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go faster.
questions.explanation: Your lane position helps you avoid other drivers' blind spots, see and be seen, and set up for turns. It is not meant to help you go faster.

questions.question: Which of the following do you NOT need to check before riding your motorcycle?

options.text: Test both brake controls to make sure the brake light turns on.
Check that the paint is not scratched.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the paint is not scratched.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tire pressure and condition, oil and fluid levels, and make sure your headlight, taillight, signal lights, and brake light all work.

questions.question: What is the best way to be seen at an intersection?

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Always ride with your headlight on.
Ride close to vehicles in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Ride with your headlight on and position your motorcycle so oncoming traffic can see you clearly. Keep space around you to avoid hazards. Do not count on eye contact alone—drivers may not notice you.

questions.question: How do medications for headaches, colds, and hay fever usually affect you?

options.text: They make you unable to concentrate.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make you drowsy.
questions.explanation: Most headache, cold, hay fever, and allergy medications can make you drowsy and affect your riding ability. Know how any medication affects you before riding.

questions.question: If you shift into a lower gear while going too fast, what can happen?

options.text: The motorcycle could jerk and the rear tire could skid.
The motorcycle could speed up suddenly.
The front tire will likely skid.
The engine will make a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle could jerk and the rear tire could skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift to a lower gear while going too fast, the motorcycle will jerk and the rear wheel may skid.

questions.question: Should you follow vehicles at a different distance at night than during the day?

options.text: Yes, keep a longer distance at night.
No, keep a shorter distance at night.
No, always keep the same distance.
No, following distance does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, keep a longer distance at night.
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to judge distance because you cannot see shadows and light contrasts. Keep a longer following distance at night than during the day.

questions.question: In New Hampshire, at what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is a person age 21 or older considered legally intoxicated?
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: A BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. Riding a motorcycle while intoxicated is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Which choice will help you be more visible on your motorcycle?

options.text: Add extra lights to your motorcycle.
Do not use your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Add extra lights to your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright or reflective clothing, add extra lights to your motorcycle, use your turn signals, and flash your brake light when needed.

questions.question: What does making eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: It guarantees they will yield to you.
It is not worth the effort.
It does not guarantee they will yield to you.
It means they know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not guarantee they will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume that eye contact with a driver means they will properly yield to you. Do not rely on eye contact alone.

questions.question: How should a group of riders pass another vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: One at a time.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane highway, riders must pass one at a time. The second rider should wait until the first rider is safely back in the original lane before passing.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Move onto the shoulder to get out of their way.
Speed up to put distance between you and them.
Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes safely and let them pass. Speeding up can be dangerous and may encourage them to follow even faster.

questions.question: What color is a warning sign?

options.text: Yellow with black lettering or symbols

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow with black lettering or symbols
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road hazards.

questions.question: What gear best protects a motorcycle rider?

options.text: A jacket that leaves the arms exposed
Shoes that stop below the ankle

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather gloves
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely. Boots or shoes should be tall and cover your ankles. Use low heels so they don't catch on the foot pegs. Leather gloves protect your hands in a crash and give you a better grip on the controls.

questions.question: Why should you practice using convex mirrors on your motorcycle?

options.text: Most people aren't used to using mirrors
They make items look farther away than they really are
They make items look closer than they really are
It's hard to remember to look at mirrors while riding

questions.correctAnswerText: They make items look farther away than they really are
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors give you a wider view of the road behind you. However, they make objects appear farther away than they actually are. Practice using them to get comfortable with this difference.

questions.question: What is true about most motorcycle crashes?

options.text: They happen at speeds over 35 mph
They are caused by worn tires
They involve riders with less than six months of experience

questions.correctAnswerText: They involve riders with less than six months of experience
questions.explanation: Be extra careful when riding a new or unfamiliar motorcycle. Most crashes happen to riders who have been riding their motorcycle for less than six months.

questions.question: If someone drank eight alcoholic drinks four hours ago, how many drinks likely remain in their body? (The body eliminates one drink per hour.)
questions.correctAnswerText: Four drinks
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals four drinks remaining in the body.
